newsitem.title: USA: Digi falls after another warning issued.
newsitem.headline: Digi falls after another warning issued.

text.p: Shares of Digi International Inc closed more than 13 percent lower on Thursday and analysts said the company's projection of lower-than-expected revenues was the latest in a recent rash of problems.
"It's going to take quite a while before investors are assured they're moving in the right direction," said Frank McEvoy, an analyst with John G. Kinnard & Co.
Late Wednesday, Digi said it expects to report revenues for its fiscal first quarter in the $42.0 million to $42.5 million range, versus $43.7 million last year.
Digi provides data communications hardware and software.
The company also said it expected to report an operating loss for the quarter, excluding AetherWorks Corp.
In December, the company projected earnings would be lower than expected and analysts said at the time the company had indicated revenues for the quarter would be about $50 milion.
"I thought they might be lower, but I was surprised it would be by this much," McEvoy said.
In December, Digi adjusted its fiscal 1996 profit to $9.3 million, or $0.69 a share, down from $14.8 million or $1.10 a share previously reported.
The company said the change included an adjustment in Digi's accounting treatment of AetherWorks Corp, a development-stage company in which Digi owns a stake.
Following that announcement, a class action lawsuit was filed against the company charging officers misrepresented and omitted information that resulted in overstated financial results.
Earlier this month, Digi said its chief executive Ervin Kamm resigned and vice president Jerry Dusa was appointed as acting chief executive.
"I think this is a company where financial reporting systems must be improved before investors can be comfortable with the company," said Amar Senan, an analyst with Volpe, Welty & Co.
Shares of Digi closed 1-1/4 lower at eight.
